public_rationale: The November 4, 2024 study reports out-of-distribution physics failures, perfect generalization within the training distribution, and measurable scaling for combinatorial generalization in its tested models [e3]. Sora's December 9, 2024 system card describes generated captions for visual training data, leaving its fit with exclusively sensory learning unclear [e4]. These items do not establish repeated failures of the sensory-learning hypothesis, including a qualifying Sora setup, during the February–December 10, 2024 observation period [e3, e4].
limitations: The controlled study tests a restricted family of models and physical situations; it does not establish the general limits of sensory learning [e3].
The packet does not isolate sensory learning itself as the cause of failure or establish a sequence of qualifying Sora evaluations [e3, e4].
Sora's use of captions leaves the meaning of 'purely from sense data' consequential to the assessment [e4].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The idea that AI can learn physics purely from sense data keeps failing, and Sora is the latest example.

statement.excerpt: The John Locke hypothesis that you can learn physics purely from sense data is failing, over, and over, and over again; this time perhaps (if I had to guess) to the tune of a billion dollars.
statement.document_title: Sora still appears to have trouble with physics

from_speaker: learn physics purely from sense data
is failing, over, and over, and over again
our_interpretation: Read as an observation about repeated attempts available by December 2024, rather than a forecast that sensory learning can never succeed.
Learning physics means acquiring reliable physical behavior that generalizes beyond familiar examples; it does not require learning every physical law.
The February-to-December Sora discussion supplies the observation window, although the wider history of repeated attempts is unspecified.
The billion-dollar aside is expressly a guess. It is not treated as a firm spending claim or included in the outcome.
Purely from sense data could mean exclusively sensory training inputs, or learning without explicit physical rules. Those readings require different evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Training descriptions and evaluations establish repeated failures to acquire reliable, generalizable physics from sensory observations, including a Sora training setup that fits the claimed sensory-learning approach.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable sensory-learning systems demonstrate robust physical generalization across varied unfamiliar situations, or evidence establishes that the asserted repeated failures did not occur.

evidence.explanation: Controlled video-learning experiments support the narrower claim that physical generalization remained unreliable. The same result reports successful learning within the training distribution, limiting any inference that sensory learning simply fails.

evidence.locator: Introduction, Overview of Sora, paragraph about recaptioning
evidence.explanation: Sora's documented training uses generated language alongside visual data. Its failures therefore do not constitute a clean test of learning exclusively from sensory inputs, although they remain relevant to learning without explicit physical rules.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A settled definition of sensory-only learning and a reliability threshold, plus documented training setups and controlled evaluations of systems available during February–December 10, 2024, including Sora. Those evaluations would need to establish repeated qualifying failures or robust physical generalization across varied unfamiliar situations.
